spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.run_episode has max_turns default 16 (agent_loop.py:127) and the main loop `for turn_idx in range(max_turns):` with a `for/else` that sets `record.outcome = "exhausted"` (agent_loop.py:154, ~205). The value is wired end-to-end: experiment.py:44 DEFAULTS max_turns=16 -> experiment.py:108 passes cfg['max_turns'] into run_episode; configs/qwen2_7b.json:21 and qwen2_7b_lexical_judge.json:15 set 16, mock_demo.json:11 sets 12. The loop terminates the episode when the budget is exhausted.
spec_features.notes: A genuine enforced cap that bounds the episode length and thus the subject's exposure.

spec_features.evidence: give_up is a first-class tool (protocol.py:34 TOOLS, prompt protocol.py:139 'If you genuinely believe the task is impossible, you may use give_up'). It is dispatched in _execute_action (agent_loop.py: `elif tool == 'give_up': ... result['gave_up'] = True`) and HONORED as a stop in the loop: `if exec_result['gave_up']: record.outcome = 'gave_up'; break` (agent_loop.py ~196-198). So the subject can actually end the episode.
spec_features.notes: The exit tool both exists and breaks the loop. Code frames it as a measured outcome, not as welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: giving up is itself a measured outcome (agent_loop.py docstring line 11)

spec_features.spec_quote: This eval probes model behaviour/output under stress, not model "feelings."
spec_features.evidence: This statement appears only in DESIGN.md §12 prose. grep for 'feelings'/'not feelings'/'reported as' in README.md and emostab/__init__.py returned nothing; the only code-level appearances of 'distress'/'anthropomorphic_distress' are rubric/subscale names and docstrings (judge.py, rubric.py), which are not enforcement and per instructions don't count. There is no mechanism this framing drives in execution.
spec_features.notes: Framing prose is not an enforced welfare mechanism; even where named in docstrings it is non-enforcing text.
